name: Molotow Jass
description: Molotow Jass is a Swiss Jass game for four players, derived from Mittlere Jass. It uses the same dynamic trump determination (first void play establishes trumps) but adapts the scoring for four players. The game features unique scoring where the middle two players can end up with potatoes while the highest and lowest scorers get sticks.

history.origins: Molotow Jass was derived from Mittlere Jass (for three players) to accommodate four players. The game preserves the dynamic trump mechanism while adapting the middle-score concept to four players.
timeline: Traditional: Developed from Mittlere Jass within Swiss Jass tradition
Modern: Played in Swiss Jass circles as a four-player alternative
Present: Part of the Swiss Jass repertoire
history.cultural: Part of the rich Swiss Jass tradition. Jass is considered the national card game of Switzerland, with many regional and player-count variants.
history.evolution: The adaptation from three to four players required significant changes to the scoring system while maintaining the core dynamic trump mechanic.

setup.deck: 36-card Jass deck (6 through Ace in four suits: Acorns, Shields, Flowers, Bells). Can use standard deck with 5s and below removed.
setup.dealing: 9 cards to each player, dealt in packets of 3. Deal and play are anticlockwise.
setup.equipment: 36-card Jass deck or modified standard deck, scoring slate (for sticks and potatoes).

rules.objective: Avoid being in the middle scores. Score points by winning tricks, but try to be either highest or lowest scorer.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads to first trick. Must follow suit if possible. If unable to follow, may play any card - if no trump is established, this card's suit becomes trumps. Once trump is established, must follow suit or trump if void.
keyRules: Different scoring than Mittlere for four players
No penalty for taking no tricks

strategy.basic: Try to be either the highest scorer or the lowest scorer. Avoid the middle. Be careful not to reach 100 points which carries a heavy penalty.
strategy.intermediate: Control when trumps are established. Win early tricks to control play. In four players, coordination is harder but watch for opportunities to force others into the middle.
strategy.advanced: Track all cards to predict trump establishment. Calculate risk of reaching 100 points. Understand when to push for high score vs. when to dump points.
tips: 100 points is the danger zone - avoid it at all costs
Sometimes taking no tricks is better than taking middle points
Establishing trumps early gives you control but reveals information
Watch opponents' scores to predict their strategies

scoring.description: Scoring uses sticks (good) and potatoes (bad). The four-player scoring differs significantly from Mittlere.
scoring.winCondition: Player with most sticks (or fewest potatoes) after agreed number of hands wins.
